newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds lawsuit jury resumes deliberations.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds lawsuit jury resumes deliberations.

text.p: Jurors resumed deliberations Monday in a lawsuit against the R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co that alleges the company was negligent in the death of a Florida smoker.

By 1200 EDT 1600 (GMT) Monday, the panel of five women and one man had deliberated for five hours over two days but had not reached a verdict. They have not sent any notes to the judge, asked no questions and requested no further information.
Court officials said the jurors had decided to have lunch sent in so they could continue working.
The jury was deciding a lawsuit filed by plaintiff Dana Raulerson, whose sister Jean Connor died of lung cancer in 1995 at age 49. The trial was in its fifth week.
The jury has been asked to decide whether Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holding Corp, negligently contributed to Connor's death and whether it manufactured a dangerous and defective product.
If jurors answer yes to those questions, they will be asked to decide on the amount of compensatory damages, whether punitive damages are in order and the amount of punitive damages.
Lawyers for the two sides were not at the courthouse but were waiting for the verdict at their offices.
